questions.question: 18 binders bind 900 books in 10 days. How many binders will be required to bind 600 books in 12 days?
questions.questionHtml: 18 binders bind 900 books in 10 days. How many binders will be required to bind 600 books in 12 days?
questions.solution:
Efficiency of each binders = 900 ÷ (18 × 10) = 5 books per hour

Now, the number of required binders to bind 600 books in 12 days ⇒ 600 ÷ (12 × 5) = 10

questions.question: Two person A and B can do a work in 60 days and 40 days respectively. They started the work together but A left after some time and B finished the remaining work in 10 days. After how many days A leave?
questions.questionHtml: Two person A and B  can do a work in 60 days and 40 days respectively. They started the work together but A left after some time and B finished the remaining work in 10 days. After how many days A leave?
questions.solution:
LCM of 60 and 40 = 120 units = Total work

Efficiency of A = 120/60 ⇒ 2 units/days

Efficiency of B = 120/40 ⇒ 3 units/days

Remaining work completed by B alone = 3 × 10 days = 30 units 

So, time taken by A and B together work 

⇒ Total work = (120 – 30) / (2 + 3) ⇒ 18 days

questions.question: 5 men & 4 women can do a piece of work in 10 days, and 4 men & 7 women can do the same work in 8 days. Find the number of days taken by 11 women to do the same work
questions.questionHtml: 5 men & 4 women can do a piece of work in 10 days, and 4 men & 7 women can do the same work in 8 days. Find the number of days taken by 11 women to do the same work
questions.solution:
Given:

5 men + 4 women can complete the work in 10 days.

4 women + 7 men can do the same work in 8 days.

Formula Used

(M1× D1× H1)/W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2)/W2

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of man be M and efficiency of woman be W

(5M + 4W) × 10 = (4M + 7W) × 8

⇒ 50M + 40W = 32M + 56W

⇒ 18M = 16W

⇒ M = (8/9)W       ----(1)     

Again, one day work of 5 men & 4 women

5M +  4W = 1/10

⇒ 5 × (8/9)W + 4W = 1/10

⇒ W [\({40 \over 9 }+ 4\)] = 1/10

⇒ W\((40+36) \over 9\)= \(1\over10\)

⇒ W = 9/760

Hence, one day work of 11 women

⇒ 11 × 9/760 = 99/760

∴ 11 women can complete the same work in \(7\frac{67}{99}\) days.

questions.question: A and B can do a certain work in 27 days and 36 days, respectively. A worked for a few days and then B joined him. They together worked till the completion of the work. If the work got completed in a total of 18 days, then for how many days did A and B work together?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a certain work in 27 days and 36 days, respectively. A worked for a few days and then B joined him. They together worked till the completion of the work. If the work got completed in a total of 18 days, then for how many days did A and B work together?
questions.solution:
Given:

Days in which A can complete the work = 27 days

Days in which B can complete the work = 36 days

Days after which total work was completed = 18 days

Formula:

Efficiency = Total work / Time taken to complete work individually

Calculation:

LCM of 27, 36, 18 = 108

Assuming that the total work is 108 units.

Efficiency of A-

⇒ \(108\over 27\) = 4 units of work/day

Efficiency of B-

⇒ \(108\over 36\) = 3 unit of work/day

Total work done in 18 days by A working alone = 4 units × 18 = 72 units

Remaining work = 108 - 72 = 36 units

Time taken by B to complete 36 units of work = \(36\over 3\) = 12 days

∴ A and B worked for 12 days.

questions.question: A, B and C individually can complete a work in 12, 10 and 15 days, respectively. All three work together and after 3 days, B and C leave the work. The remaining work will be completed by A in:
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C individually can complete a work in 12, 10 and 15 days, respectively. All three work together and after 3 days, B and C leave the work. The remaining work will be completed by A in:
questions.solution:
Given:

A, B and C individually can complete a work in 12, 10 and 15 days respectively

All three work together and after 3 days, B and C leave the work.

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency × Total Time

Calculation:

LCM (12, 10, 15) = 60

Let the total work be 60 units (∵ LCM of 12, 10, 15 = 60)

Efficiency of A = 60/12 = 5 units/day

Efficiency of B = 60/10 = 6 units/day

Efficiency of C = 60/15 = 4 units/day

Work done in 3 days by A, B, C = 3 × (5 + 6 + 4) = 45 units

Time required by A to complete the remaining work

⇒ (60 - 45)/5 = 3 days

∴ The remaining work will be completed by A in 3 days.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 28 days. B is 68% more efficient than A. Find the number of days taken by B to do the same piece of work.
questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 28 days. B is 68% more efficient than A. Find the number of days taken by B to do the same piece of work.
questions.solution:
Efficiency of B = 168 units (68% more than A)

Work done by B in 1 day = (1/28) × (168/100) = 3/50

Days taken by B = 1 / (3/50) = 50/3

questions.question: A can complete 25% of the work in 4 days, B can complete 50% of the same work in 12 days and C can complete the same work in 32 days. They started working together but C left after 4 days of the start and A left 6 days before the completion of the work. In how many days was the work completed?
questions.questionHtml: A can complete 25% of the work in 4 days, B can complete 50% of the same work in 12 days and C can complete the same work in 32 days. They started working together but C left after 4 days of the start and A left 6 days before the completion of the work. In how many days was the work completed?
questions.solution:
Given:

A 25% work in 4 days.

B 50% work in 12 days.

C 100% work in 32 days.

Formula Used: 

Work Done = Time × Efficiency

Calculation: 

A 100% work in 16 days. 

B 100% work in 24 days.

C 100% work in 32 days.

Total Work Done = LCM(16,24,32) = 96

Efficiency of A = 6

Efficiency of B = 4

Efficiency of C = 3

⇒ (A + B + C) × 4 + (A + B) × (x - 10) + (6) × B = 96

 ⇒ 13 × 4 + 10 × ( x - 10)  + 6 × 4 = 96

⇒ 52 + 10x - 100 + 24 = 96

 ⇒ 76 + 10x - 100 = 96

 ⇒ 10x - 24 = 96

 ⇒  x = 12 

 ∴ The correct answer is 12 days.

∴ The Option 2 is correct.

questions.question: Five men can do a work in 12 days while 10 women can do the same work in 8 days. In how many days can 3 men and 4 women together complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: Five men can do a work in 12 days while 10 women can do the same work in 8 days. In how many days can 3 men and 4 women together complete the work?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total work = 5M × 12 = 10W × 8 ⇒ 60M = 80W.

Efficiency ratio (M/W) = 80 ÷ 60 = 4/3.

Total work = 60 × 4 = 240 units.

Time taken by 3M and 4W = 240 ÷ (3 × 4 + 4 × 3) = 240 ÷ 24 = 10.

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ 5 men can complete the work in 12 days.

⇒ 1 man can complete the work in 5 × 12 = 60 days.

⇒ 10 women can complete the work in 8 days.

⇒ 1 woman can complete the work in 10 × 8 = 80 days.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
1 Man 60 240 4
1 Woman 80 3

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of 1 man = 4 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of 1 woman = 3 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of 3 men and 4 women = (3 × 4) + (4 × 3) = 12 + 12 = 24 units/day

⇒ Time taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 240 ÷ 24 = 10 days

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Additional Information

Chain Rule (MDH Concept)

If M1 persons can do W1 work in D1 days working H1 hours per day, then M1D1H1 ÷ W1 = M2D2H2 ÷ W2.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If people work for the same number of days, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

This topic works on the exact same logic as Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, and outlet pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency.

questions.question: If m persons can paint a house in d days, how many days will it take for (m + 2) persons to paint the same house ?
questions.questionHtml: If m persons can paint a house in d days, how many days will it take for (m + 2) persons to paint the same house ?
questions.solution:
Given:

m persons paint a house in d days.

Concpet:

(M1 × D1 × H1)/W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2)/W2

Calculation:

Let, (m + 2) person can paint the house in y days.

Using the above formula

m × d = (m + 2) × y

⇒ y = \((\frac{md}{m + 2})\) days

∴ (m + 2) persons paint a house in \((\frac{md}{m + 2})\) days.

questions.question: A.B and C are assigned to complete a work. If the ratio of time taken by A, B and C is 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 6. Find the ratio of their efficiency.
questions.questionHtml: A.B and C are assigned to complete a work. If the ratio of time taken by A, B and C is 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 6. Find the ratio of their efficiency.
questions.solution: The ratio of the efficiency of A, B, and C = 1/4: 1/3 : 1/6 = 3: 4: 2
